item.title: Identity
item.description: Overview Identity is an algebraic property of a set relative to an operation.

item.title: Null Space
item.description: Overview The null space of a linear transformation from one vector space to another, is the subset of the first vector space consisting of all vectors that the transformation maps to zero in the codomain.

item.title: Invertibility
item.description: Overview Invertibility is an algebraic property of an element relative to a binary operation.

item.title: Group
item.description: Overview A group is an algebraic structure consisting of a set equipped and a binary operation that is associative and closed, has an Identity element and for which every element admits an Invertibility.

item.title: Linear Combination
item.description: Overview A linear combination \large V is a sum of scalar multiples of vectors defined as \large V = av + bw where \large a, b are scalars and \large v, w are vectors.

item.title: Polynomial
item.description: Overview A polynomial is an algebraic object defined as the finite sum of powers of a variable multiplied by coefficients, for which there is only one coefficient per power such that (a_0 + a_1X + a_2X^2 + ..

item.title: Ring
item.description: AlgebraicStructure A ring is a type of algebraic structure. It consist of a set with two operations.

item.title: Vector Space
item.description: Overview A vector space is an algebraic structure defined as a set \large V together with two operations called vector addition (which combines two vectors) and scalar multiplication (which scales a vector by a scalar).

item.title: Column Space
item.description: Overview The column space of a linear equation matrix is the space of possible outputs/solutions to the system of equations for that matrix.

item.title: Linear Transformation
item.description: Overview A linear transformation is a function that takes a vector as input and produces another vector in the same or a different vector space.
